dedupe_keys.name: noaa navigation response teams reopen texas ports after hurricane harvey 2017

description: This Office of Coast Survey update describes how NOAA helped Texas ports recover after Hurricane Harvey, which made landfall as a Category 4 storm on 25 August 2017. Before landfall, Coast Survey prepositioned two navigation response teams, small survey vessels with three-person crews, to carry out surveys prioritised by the US Coast Guard with the Army Corps of Engineers, ports, terminal operators and state and local responders, and placed navigation managers at the incident command centres in Houston and Galveston and at Coast Guard Sector Corpus Christi. Team 2 surveyed Corpus Christi Pass with side scan sonar, including a drill ship that broke loose and lost a 90-foot crane boom, and helped verify new synthetic (virtual) aids to navigation used when buoys cannot be placed fast enough; after this work the Captain of the Port reopened the port to deep draft vessels with restrictions. Team 4 could not reach its boat until floodwaters receded, then surveyed the Galveston Ship Channel and Bolivar anchorages, while a mobile survey unit and a contractor vessel joined. Coverage: Texas Gulf ports. Access: a public web update. Licence and cost: US government work, free. Caveats: an operational news account without reopening times for each port. It illustrates emergency response and recovery of ports, where channel surveys gate reopening. It relates to the post-hurricane supply chain case study, Marine Cadastre AIS data and OpenSeaMap in the catalogue.
